senses.gloss: (cmp. מִנְהָג) practice, adopted opinion, rule.—ה׳ כ־ in practice, the opinion of … is the rule.
units: Keth. 77ᵃ ה׳ כמותו; a. v. fr.—ה׳ למשה מסיני a usage dating from Moses as delivered from Sinai, i.e. a traditional law or a traditional interpretation of a written law.

<cite ref="Mishnah Orlah 3:9">Orl. III, 9</cite> <he>הערלה ה׳</he> the application of the laws of Orlah (v. <cite ref="P01387"><he>עָרְלָה</he></cite>) outside of Palestine is traditional or a custom (<he>הילכות מדינה</he>, v.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 2:1:3">Y. Bets. II, 61ᵇ</cite> top <he>לה׳</he> as a traditional opinion (of a teacher), opp. <he>לעובדא</he> as his own decision for practice.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 3:4:9">Y. Dem. III, 23ᶜ</cite> bot., sq. <he>מה׳</he> according to a custom.

<cite ref="Keritot 13b:47">Ker. 13ᵇ</cite> ‘which the Lord has spoken’ (<cite ref="Leviticus 10:11">Lev. X, 11</cite>) <he>זו ה׳</he> that means traditional interpretations. Ib. III, 9 (15ᵇ) <he>אם ה׳ נקבל אם לדין וכ׳</he> if it is a tradition, we must accept it, but if it is a logical inference, there may be an objection to it.
<cite ref="Berakhot 31a:22">Ber. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>מתוך דבר ה׳</he> from discussion about a law, opp. <he>ה׳ פסוקה</he> a decision arrived at after discussion.
<cite ref="Berakhot 47b:13">Ib. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>המחדדין … בה׳</he> who whet each other’s wits in legal discussion.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 82a:3">Snh. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>נתעלמה ממנו ה׳</he> the law had escaped his memory.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 82a:3">Ib.</cite> <he>ראה … ונזכר ה׳</he> he saw an act and recalled the law; a. v. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="E00567"><he>הֲלָכוֹת</he></cite>, constr. <cite ref="E00567"><he>הִלְכוֹת</he></cite>, <cite ref="E00570"><he>הִילְ׳</he></cite>. Kidd. l. c. <he>הי׳ מדינה</he> (v. R. S. to <cite ref="Mishnah Orlah 3:9">Orl. III, 9</cite>; ed. <he>הלכתא מדינה</he>, corr. acc.) the usages of the country (outside of Palestine).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 3:5:12">Y. Hor. III, end, 48ᶜ</cite> <he>אילו ה׳</he> that means the collections of laws (Mishnah).
<cite ref="Temurah 14b:49">Tem. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>כותבי ה׳</he> those who reduce traditions (oral law) to writing.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 67b:12">Snh. 67ᵇ</cite> <he>הי׳ כשפים</he> the laws concerning the punishment of witchcraft.
Sabb. 32ᵃ; Tosef. ib. II, 10; a. v. fr.—[הלכה in Talmud Y., heading of Mishnah, in Talm. Bab. מתני׳.]
